candidates.text: The Government of the United States has broad, undoubted power over the subject of immigration and the status of aliens
candidates.speaker: Kennedy
phrases: broad, undoubted power over the subject of immigration

candidates.text: Where Congress occupies an entire field, as it has in the field of alien registration, even complementary state regulation is impermissible
candidates.speaker: Kennedy
phrases: even complementary state regulation is impermissible

candidates.text: Under the Supremacy Clause, pre-emptive effect is to be given to congressionally enacted laws, not to judicially divined legislative purposes
candidates.speaker: Thomas
phrases: not to judicially divined legislative purposes

candidates.text: The National Government has significant power to regulate immigration. With power comes responsibility
candidates.speaker: Kennedy
phrases: the State may not pursue policies that undermine federal law

candidates.text: Arizona has moved to protect its sovereignty---not in contradiction of federal law, but in complete compliance with it
candidates.speaker: Scalia
phrases: we should cease referring to it as a sovereign State
